newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, recovering well, could visit Kremlin soon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, recovering well, could visit Kremlin soon.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin could return to the Kremlin for brief visits as early as next week, Interfax news agency quoted his chief doctor as saying on Thursday.

Sergei Mironov said Yeltsin, 65, was recovering smoothly from the quintuple heart bypass operation carried out on November 5 to improve the blood supply to his heart and to enable him to lead a normal life.
But the president, who still favours home-made pelmeni dumplings for lunch, was being asked not to eat fatty foods or items containing large amounts of cholesterol, Mironov said.
He said doctors would decide next week whether Yeltsin, who is being treated in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, could move to his official residence in the same compound.
"It is possible that after December 5 the president will make a few test visits to the Kremlin from Barvikha," Mironov said.
Yeltsin, dogged by ill health, has spent very little time in the Kremlin since he was re-elected for a second term on July 3.

Mironov said Yeltsin would probably stay at Barvikha for two or three more weeks. He was already holding two or three working meetings each day, working on documents for about four hours and walking for up to one km (more than half a mile).
"Of course the doctors do not really want him to go that far yet, but Boris Nikolayevich was and still is, to put it mildly, not exactly an obedient patient," he said.
He added: "We hope that after December 15-20 Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) will be able to work at the Kremlin practically at his normal rhythm."
